deep_dive.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology via Topology-Informed Graph Attention and Gene-Semantics Conditioning
deep_dive.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) profiles gene expression with spatial context but remains costly, motivating models that infer expression from H&E images. Existing approaches face three key limitations: (i) a single patch embedding is often insufficient: morphologically similar regions can exhibit distinct expression due to spatial context, while naive neighborhood aggregation can over-smooth boundaries; (ii) conventional fixed, gene-indexed output heads treat genes independently and cannot directly support strict zero-shot prediction for unseen genes; and (iii) common metrics under-measure spatial pattern fidelity and boundary resolution. To address these challenges, we propose TIGEM, a topology-informed, gene-conditioned framework for histology-to-ST inference. TIGEM learns topology-aware spot representations by regularizing graph attention with tissue-level topology and morphology cues to avoid cross-compartment smoothing, and uses gene semantic modulation to replace gene-indexed heads, enabling zero-shot prediction for unseen genes. We also introduce Graph Spectral Correlation (GSC) to evaluate spatial pattern fidelity and boundary resolution complement to PCC/MSE. Across three large-scale ST datasets, TIGEM achieves overall state-of-the-art performance and significantly improved boundary prediction resolution, and further demonstrates the ability to predict expression patterns for genes unseen during training, extending prior zero-shot histology-to-ST efforts with topology-aware spatial propagation and PLM-based gene conditioning.

deep_dive.title: Where single-cell foundation models help: a public-data benchmark of annotation, in silico perturbation and gene regulatory inference
deep_dive.abstract: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network inference. We benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), four newer FMs, CellOracle, supervised perturbation models and task-matched simple baselines on public data, from Perturb-seq screens of cell lines and primary T cells to a brain organoid screen, the developing mouse cortex and lung cancer biopsies, under an analysis plan fixed before the new results. FMs helped most when labels were transferred across species: Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy from human to mouse lung, above every baseline (at most 0.94), and fine-tuned Geneformer V2 reached macro-F1 0.88 from mouse to human, against at most 0.74. In K562, zero-shot perturbations captured the direction of real responses (up to 76% of perturbations), Geneformer V2 tracked CRISPRa effect sizes with its overexpression protocol (rho = 0.30), and its networks recovered tumour differential expression better than co-expression. Within a species, FM embeddings did not exceed principal components. In silico deletions followed target expression and, across seven screens with replicate-level ground truth, met the predefined criterion in none of 81 tests, although in K562 and RPE1 the measured effects replicated between libraries. In contrast, the gene vectors of seven of eight FMs, including three newer models, added to expression features, predicted which knockdowns have large effects in an independent genome-wide K562 screen (rho between 0.34 and 0.44, against 0.26 with expression alone). We release the benchmark and its checks as the fmaudit package.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 单细胞基础模型被宣传为注释、计算机扰动和基因调控网络推断的通用工具，但缺乏公正系统的评估。作者在公共数据上对五个基础模型、四个新模型、CellOracle、监督扰动模型及简单基线进行统一基准测试，覆盖Perturb-seq细胞系与原代T细胞、脑类器官、发育中小鼠皮层和肺癌活检。结果显示基础模型主要在跨物种标签迁移时占优，而计算机扰动等任务收益有限，为用户选择工具提供了实证依据。

quick_skim.title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
quick_skim.abstract: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image model (0.299--0.371 \vs 0.214--0.232), and paired tests separate three tiers among the pathology models. Unlike a supervised probe, BioScore needs no labels, builds its reference from the data and scores even from few sections, yet it ranks the encoders as a probe does. Its per-identity breakdown indicates which cell identities each encoder captures or misses.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: benchmark linking pathology image encoders with spatial transcriptomics cell identities

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: BioScore benchmarks pathology image encoders by measuring how specifically sparse features of patch embeddings follow spatial transcriptomics-defined cell identities, offering a biology-aware alternative to task-performance benchmarks.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 病理基础模型通常以分类、检索等下游任务比较，难以反映其表征所蕴含的生物学信息。作者提出BioScore基准，用稀疏自编码器将图像块嵌入分解为稀疏特征并聚类，再以同组织空间转录组为参考，衡量各特征群对52种标记基因定义细胞身份的特异性。由于自编码器训练完全无监督，匹配结果可反映编码器真实的细胞身份感知能力。该基准为病理图像与基因表达的多模态评估提供了生物学视角。
